title: SoftBank’s debt-fuelled AI bet faces its reckoning at earnings
excerpt: SoftBank’s earnings will be flattered by OpenAI, but the focus is how Masayoshi Son will fund tens of billions in AI commitments as debt matures.
content_html:
SoftBank’s AI bet meets its accountants this week. When the Japanese group reports earnings, the headline profit will look healthy, but the real story is the mountain of funding commitments Masayoshi Son has stacked behind OpenAI.

Analysts expect net profit of around ¥148bn, close to $940m, for the April-to-June quarter, flattered by the rising value of its OpenAI stake. The number investors will actually study is how Son intends to pay for what he has promised.

The promises are enormous. SoftBank has committed more than $60bn to OpenAI and related AI infrastructure, and it is racing to meet a near-term tranche of roughly $22.5bn to OpenAI by the end of the year.

The bill arrives as debt matures. SoftBank faces about $30bn of obligations in the second half of 2026, including a $40bn bridging loan that runs to March 2027 and a $20bn margin loan secured against its Arm shares.

One funding route has jammed. A plan to borrow against its OpenAI stake stalled as lenders grew wary of credit backed by a private company, and SoftBank has already cut a related margin-loan target.

The leverage is the crux. S&P Global put SoftBank’s loan-to-value ratio at 33% in March, well above the 17% the company prefers to cite, though it expects the figure to ease as asset values move.

Son is unmoved by the worry. He has called bubble talk absurd and predicts AI will cost $5tn a year by 2040, a scale on which SoftBank’s current borrowing looks, to him, like a down payment.

He has kept the financing coming. SoftBank lined up a new $60bn bond to keep the OpenAI bet funded, part of a leverage stack that grows more elaborate with each round.

SoftBank is no stranger to enormous bets. Its Vision Funds poured tens of billions into startups with famously mixed results, and the OpenAI wager is the largest single expression of Son’s conviction yet.

Its stake in the chip designer Arm has become the anchor for much of this. The prized asset is now pledged against the borrowing that funds the AI push, tying SoftBank’s most valuable holding to its riskiest bet.

The value of the prize is itself contested. OpenAI is reported to be chasing a $1tn IPO valuation, up from $852bn, while sceptics put its true worth closer to $300bn, a gap that swings SoftBank’s paper gains wildly.

The Street is mostly still on board. Fifteen of twenty sell-side analysts kept buy ratings this month, betting that Son’s access to capital and the OpenAI upside outweigh the strain on the balance sheet.

The bears see a chain reaction. A drop in asset prices could tighten SoftBank’s liquidity, and rising Chinese competition could squeeze OpenAI’s margins and the chip demand the whole thesis rests on.

There is history in the caution. SoftBank has ridden Son’s convictions to spectacular wins and equally spectacular losses before, and the scale of the current bet leaves less room for the second than any he has made.

There is a circularity critics keep pointing to. SoftBank borrows to fund OpenAI, whose rising value underpins those very loans, so a wobble in one leg of the structure quickly travels to the others.

That is why this earnings call is more than a scorecard. Investors want a credible plan for the year-end commitments, not just a profit line lifted by a mark-to-market gain on a stake that has not been sold.

Son has wagered the group’s balance sheet on being right about AI, and about OpenAI in particular. The earnings will not settle that bet, but they will show how much rope he has left before the market asks him to prove it.

content_html_zh:
软银的人工智能赌注本周将与会计师见面。 当这家日本集团公布财报时，总体利润看起来很健康，但真正的情况是孙正义在 OpenAI 背后投入了大量资金。

分析师预计 4 月至 6 月当季净利润约为 1,480 亿日元（约合 9.4 亿美元），这得益于其 OpenAI 股份价值的不断上涨。 投资者实际研究的数字是孙正义打算如何兑现他的承诺。

这些承诺是巨大的。 软银已向 OpenAI 及相关人工智能基础设施承诺超过 600 亿美元，并且正在竞相在年底前向 OpenAI 提供约 225 亿美元的近期资金。

账单随着债务到期而到来。 软银在 2026 年下半年面临约 300 亿美元的债务，其中包括截至 2027 年 3 月的 400 亿美元过渡贷款，以及以其 Arm 股票为担保的 200 亿美元保证金贷款。

一条融资途径已经堵塞。 由于贷方对私营公司支持的信贷越来越谨慎，以 OpenAI 股份为抵押借款的计划陷入停滞，软银已经削减了相关的保证金贷款目标。

杠杆是关键。 标准普尔全球公司 (S&P Global) 将软银 3 月份的贷款与价值比率定为 33%，远高于该公司更愿意引用的 17%，不过预计随着资产价值的变动，这一数字将会下降。

儿子对担心无动于衷。 他称泡沫言论很荒谬，并预测到 2040 年人工智能每年的成本将达到 5 万亿美元，在他看来，软银目前的借款规模就像首付。

他一直在源源不断地提供融资。 软银准备发行 600 亿美元的新债券，为 OpenAI 的押注提供资金，这是杠杆堆栈的一部分，每一轮都变得更加复杂。

软银对巨额赌注并不陌生。 其愿景基金向初创公司投入了数百亿美元，但结果却喜忧参半，而 OpenAI 的赌注是迄今为止孙正义信念的最大单一体现。

它在芯片设计公司 Arm 的股份已成为这一切的支柱。 现在，这笔宝贵的资产被用来抵押为人工智能发展提供资金的借款，将软银最有价值的资产与其风险最大的押注联系起来。

该奖项的价值本身就存在争议。 据报道，OpenAI 寻求 1 万亿美元的 IPO 估值，高于 8520 亿美元，而怀疑论者认为其真实价值接近 3000 亿美元，这一差距极大地影响了软银的账面收益。

华尔街大部分仍在船上。 本月 20 名卖方分析师中有 15 名维持买入评级，认为孙正义获得资本的机会和 OpenAI 的上行空间将超过资产负债表上的压力。

空头看到了连锁反应。 资产价格下跌可能会收紧软银的流动性，而中国竞争的加剧可能会挤压 OpenAI 的利润率和整个论文所依赖的芯片需求。

警告中有历史。 软银此前曾凭借孙正义的信念取得了惊人的胜利，也曾取得过同样惨重的损失，而目前的赌注规模为第二次赌注留下的空间比他之前所做的任何一次都要小。

批评者一直指出存在循环性。 软银借钱为 OpenAI 提供资金，而 OpenAI 不断上涨的价值支撑着这些贷款，因此该结构的一个方面的动摇很快就会波及其他方面。

这就是为什么这次财报电话会议不仅仅是一个记分卡。 投资者希望有一个可靠的年终承诺计划，而不仅仅是通过未出售股份的按市值计算的收益来提高利润线。

孙正义将集团的资产负债表押注于人工智能，尤其是 OpenAI 的正确性。 收益不会解决这个赌注，但它们会显示在市场要求他证明这一点之前他还剩下多少绳索。
